name: GymOS
project:
Each organization represents a gym. The gym can create membership plans, classes, and trainers. Some classes or plans can remain as drafts or be inactive.
On the customer route, members can view only active plans and available classes, create bookings, and see their own bookings. On the organization route, staff can manage plans, classes, trainers, and all member bookings.
This can test multi-tenant isolation, tenant-specific routes, user scopes, and authorization policies.
description: Multi-tenant gym SaaS with subdomain isolation and tier-restricted bookings.

current_prd.elevator_pitch: GymOS is a robust, multi-tenant SaaS platform designed for gym owners who need a fully isolated, branded space to manage their operations, and for members who want a seamless booking experience. Unlike generic management tools, GymOS provides complete tenant isolation via subdomain routing (e.g., ironworks.gymplatform.com) and enforces strict membership-tier booking restrictions. Built as a high-fidelity portfolio project, it showcases production-ready multi-tenant architecture, mock payment flows, and secure data isolation, proving how modern SaaS applications can scale securely and efficiently.
current_prd.problem_statement: Gym owners need a simple, isolated way to manage their operations, plans, and bookings under their own brand/subdomain, while members need a seamless way to view active plans, available classes, and manage bookings without cross-tenant data leakage.
current_prd.solution: A multi-tenant SaaS platform that provides subdomain-based isolation for each gym. Gym staff can manage plans, classes, trainers, and bookings on their organization route, while members can view active plans, available classes, and manage their bookings on their customer route.

key_features.feature_description: Dynamic subdomain routing (e.g., ironworks.gymplatform.com) that resolves the tenant context at the request level, ensuring strict database-level or schema-level data isolation between gyms.
A comprehensive back-office dashboard for gym staff to manage membership plans (active/draft/inactive), schedule classes, assign trainers, and view member bookings.
A branded member portal where gym members can view available classes, manage their active bookings, and track their weekly class attendance.
An automated validation engine that enforces plan-specific limits (e.g., Basic plan restricted to 2 classes/week) during the booking checkout flow.
A simulated checkout flow allowing members to select plans and complete mock payments to activate their memberships and unlock booking credits.
A central landing page and onboarding flow where new gym owners can register their gym, provision a unique subdomain, and set up their initial admin account.

current_prd.design_principles:
### 1. Clean & Modern Aesthetics
- **Minimalist Layouts**: Prioritize whitespace to reduce cognitive load, allowing users to focus on scheduling and booking tasks.
- **Consistent Typography**: Use a highly legible sans-serif typeface (e.g., Inter) with clear weight hierarchies to distinguish headings, body text, and interactive elements.

### 2. High-Contrast & Accessible Design
- **WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance**: Ensure all text-to-background contrast ratios meet or exceed 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
- **Focus States & Keyboard Navigation**: Provide highly visible focus indicators for all interactive elements to support keyboard-only and screen-reader users.
- **Color-Blind Friendly Indicators**: Never rely solely on color to convey state (e.g., use both color and icons/text labels to indicate booking status or error states).

### 3. Responsive & Mobile-First Layouts
- **Fluid Grid System**: Design with a mobile-first approach, ensuring that the class schedule, booking flows, and dashboards scale seamlessly from 320px mobile screens to ultra-wide desktop monitors.
- **Touch-Friendly Targets**: Maintain a minimum touch target size of 48x48 pixels for all interactive elements on mobile devices.

### 4. Clarity of Scheduling & Booking
- **Visual Calendar & List Views**: Present class schedules in intuitive, filterable list and calendar formats, highlighting class times, available spots, and trainer names.
- **Real-Time Limit Tracking**: Display clear, real-time indicators of the member's remaining weekly class credits (e.g., "1 of 2 classes booked this week") directly on the booking interface to prevent confusion.
- **Instant Feedback**: Provide immediate, clear visual feedback for successful bookings, limit-reached errors, and loading states.

user_stories.title: Tenant Registration & Provisioning

user_story.i_want: to register my gym and provision a custom subdomain
user_story.so_that: I can have a dedicated, isolated portal for my gym operations

acceptance_criteria: Guest users can access the registration form at gymplatform.com/register without an account
The registration form requires Gym Name, Subdomain, Admin Email, and Password
The system validates that the subdomain is unique and contains only alphanumeric characters
Upon successful registration, the system provisions the tenant database schema and redirects the user to the new subdomain login page at {subdomain}.gymplatform.com/login
Only guest users can access the registration page; authenticated users are redirected to their dashboard
The data model stores description and the application uses it as described in this story.

user_stories.title: Subdomain Routing & Tenant Context Resolution

user_story.i_want: to access my gym's portal via its custom subdomain
user_story.so_that: I am routed to the correct tenant context and see the correct branding

acceptance_criteria: Guest users can access the gym's portal via a custom subdomain (e.g., ironworks.gymplatform.com)
The system resolves the tenant context at the request level based on the subdomain
If the subdomain does not exist, the system redirects the user to a 404 page or the main platform landing page
Only guest, gym_member, and gym_staff roles can access the resolved subdomain portal
The portal displays the specific gym's name and branding dynamically based on the resolved tenant context

user_stories.title: Strict Data Isolation Verification

user_story.i_want: to enforce strict database-level or schema-level isolation between tenants
user_story.so_that: no tenant can access or modify another tenant's data under any circumstances

acceptance_criteria: The system automatically appends or enforces tenant isolation filters on all database queries
Any attempt to access data belonging to another tenant ID returns an unauthorized error or a 404 Not Found
Only system can execute cross-tenant database migrations or maintenance tasks
Database connection pooling or schema switching is performed dynamically per request based on the resolved subdomain

user_stories.title: Staff Authentication & Login

user_story.i_want: to log in to my gym's staff portal
user_story.so_that: I can securely manage my gym's operations

acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing staff dashboard paths
Only gym_staff can access the staff dashboard at {subdomain}.gymplatform.com/staff/dashboard
The login form validates credentials against the specific tenant's user database
Upon successful login, the staff member is redirected to the staff dashboard
The system provides a secure logout mechanism that invalidates the session and redirects to /login

user_stories.title: Trainer Management

user_story.i_want: to manage trainers (create, read, update, delete)
user_story.so_that: I can assign them to classes and manage their schedules

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_staff can access the trainer management page at /staff/trainers
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /staff/trainers
Staff can create a trainer profile with Name, Bio, Specialty, and Email
Staff can update trainer details or delete a trainer profile if they have no active classes assigned
The system displays a list of all trainers registered under the current tenant

user_stories.title: Membership Plan Management

user_story.i_want: to manage membership plans (draft, active, inactive)
user_story.so_that: members can subscribe to them and view their details

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_staff can access the membership plan management page at /staff/plans
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /staff/plans
Staff can create a plan with Name, Price, Weekly Class Limit, and Status (Draft, Active, Inactive)
Staff can change the status of a plan; only Active plans are visible to members for subscription
The system prevents deletion of plans that have active member subscriptions

user_stories.title: Class Scheduling & Management

user_story.i_want: to manage classes (create, read, update, cancel)
user_story.so_that: members can view and book them

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_staff can access the class scheduling page at /staff/classes
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /staff/classes
Staff can schedule a class by entering Name, Trainer, Date, Time, Capacity, and Duration
Staff can cancel a class, which automatically updates its status to Cancelled and notifies booked members
The system validates that the assigned trainer is available at the scheduled time

user_stories.title: View Member Bookings & Attendance

user_story.so_that: I can manage attendance and schedules effectively

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_staff can access the bookings overview page at /staff/bookings
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /staff/bookings
Staff can view a list of all bookings filtered by class, date, or member name
Staff can mark a member's attendance status as Attended, No-Show, or Cancelled
The system displays real-time booking counts and remaining capacity for each scheduled class

user_stories.title: View Active Membership Plans

user_story.so_that: I can choose a plan that fits my needs

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can access the plans selection page at /plans
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /plans
The page displays all active membership plans with their name, price, and weekly class limit
Draft or Inactive plans are not visible to members
The system highlights the member's currently active plan if they have one

user_stories.title: View Available Classes

user_story.so_that: I can find classes to attend

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can access the class schedule page at /classes
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /classes
The schedule displays active classes with Name, Trainer, Date, Time, and remaining spots
Members can filter classes by date, trainer, or class type
Cancelled classes are clearly marked and cannot be booked

user_stories.title: Book a Class

user_story.so_that: I can reserve my spot in the session

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can book a class via the /classes page
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when attempting to book
The system validates that the class has remaining capacity before confirming the booking
Upon successful booking, the system decrements the class capacity and displays a confirmation modal
The booking is saved and visible in the member's dashboard at /dashboard/bookings

user_stories.title: Manage My Bookings

user_story.i_want: to view and manage my bookings

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can access their bookings dashboard at /dashboard/bookings
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /dashboard/bookings
Members can view a list of their upcoming and past bookings
Members can cancel an upcoming booking up to a configurable time limit (e.g., 2 hours before class)
Cancelling a booking restores the class capacity and updates the member's weekly limit count

user_stories.title: Enforce Weekly Class Limit

user_story.i_want: the system to enforce my membership plan's weekly class limit
user_story.so_that: I don't exceed my weekly allowance

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member is subject to membership-tier booking restrictions
The system calculates the number of active bookings the member has for the current calendar week
If the member attempts to book a class that exceeds their plan's weekly limit (e.g., 2 classes/week for Basic), the booking is blocked
The system displays a clear error message: 'Booking limit reached for your membership tier'
The 'Book Class' button is disabled or shows a warning if the weekly limit has already been reached

user_stories.title: Mock Payment & Subscription Activation

user_story.i_want: to complete a mock payment to activate my membership
user_story.so_that: I can unlock booking credits and start booking classes

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can access the checkout page at /checkout
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /checkout
The checkout page displays a mock payment form accepting simulated credit card details
Upon successful mock payment, the system activates the subscription and updates the member's status to Active
The system displays a success confirmation view and redirects the member to the class schedule

user_stories.title: Subscription Billing History

user_story.i_want: to view my subscription billing history
user_story.so_that: I can track my mock payments and active plan status

acceptance_criteria: Only gym_member can access the billing history page at /dashboard/billing
Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login when accessing /dashboard/billing
The page displays a list of all mock transactions with Date, Amount, Plan Name, and Status
Members can view their current active plan and next renewal date
The system allows members to cancel their active subscription, which sets it to cancel at the end of the current billing cycle

ai_requirements.guardrails:
- Multi-Tenant Isolation: Every AI request must include a validated organization_id derived from the authenticated session/subdomain. The AI service must strictly validate that all input data belongs to the requested organization_id before passing it to the LLM. Prompts must explicitly instruct the LLM to only consider the provided context and never leak or assume information outside the tenant's scope.
- Hallucination Prevention: Use strict JSON schemas (Structured Outputs / Tool Calling) to ensure the LLM returns data matching the exact API contract. Validate that recommended gym_class_ids and trainer_ids actually exist in the active database for that tenant.
- Rate Limiting: Implement rate limiting per tenant and per user (e.g., max 5 recommendation requests per member per hour, max 10 schedule optimizations per staff per day) to prevent API abuse and cost spikes.
- Fallback Behavior: If the AI service is unavailable or fails, fall back to a simple rule-based recommendation engine (e.g., recommend the most popular classes with open capacity) and display a friendly message. For schedule optimization, fall back to copying the previous week's schedule.

capabilities.name: Personalized Class Recommendations
outputs: recommended_classes (list of gym_class_ids with personalized rationales)
capabilities.trigger: Member visits the dashboard or class schedule page, or clicks 'Get Recommendations'.
capabilities.description: Recommends upcoming gym classes to members based on their attendance history, membership tier, and preferences.

capabilities.name: Automated Schedule Optimization
outputs: optimized_slots (list of recommended class slots, trainer assignments, expected booking rates, and rationales)
capabilities.trigger: Gym staff clicks 'Optimize Schedule' or 'Generate Schedule Recommendations' in the staff dashboard.
capabilities.description: Recommends optimal class times and trainer assignments for gym staff based on historical booking rates, trainer availability, and capacity.

api_contracts.purpose: Generate personalized class recommendations for a member based on their attendance history, membership tier, and preferences.
Generate an optimized class schedule and trainer assignments for a target week based on historical booking rates and trainer availability.

ai_requirements.non_functional:
- Latency: Recommendations should return within 1.5 seconds (using caching where possible). Schedule optimization can be asynchronous (returning a job ID, processing in background, and notifying staff via webhook or polling) with a target completion under 15 seconds.
- Cost: Use cost-efficient models (e.g., smaller, faster LLMs) for recommendations, and more capable models only for complex schedule optimization. Cache recommendation results for 24 hours.
- Observability: Log prompt tokens, completion tokens, latency, and tenant ID for every AI request. Track LLM error rates and fallback triggers.

data_model_links.role: Provides member preferences, status, and membership plan limits to the recommendation engine.
Provides historical attendance, no-shows, and booking rates to both recommendations and schedule optimization.
Provides available upcoming classes for recommendations, and historical class performance for schedule optimization.
Provides trainer specialties, bios, and availability for schedule optimization and trainer assignments.
Ensures strict tenant isolation; all queries and context are scoped to a specific organization_id.

ai_requirements.data_requirements:
- RAG Sources: Member profiles, historical bookings, gym classes, and trainer profiles.
- Embeddings & Vector Store: Class descriptions, trainer bios, and member preferences can be embedded. Any vector database or index MUST be strictly partitioned by organization_id (tenant ID) using metadata filtering (e.g., organization_id == tenant_id) or separate collections/namespaces per tenant to prevent cross-tenant data leakage.
- Retention: AI-generated recommendations and optimized schedules should have a configurable retention policy (e.g., cache recommendations for 24 hours, delete historical optimization logs after 30 days). No PII should be stored in external LLM provider logs (zero data retention policy with LLM vendors).
ai_requirements.service_boundaries: The AI service is a separate, dedicated microservice responsible for prompt engineering, LLM orchestration, and schedule optimization algorithms. The main application is responsible for user authentication, tenant context resolution, database access, and rendering the UI. All communication between the main application and the AI service is secured via API keys and scoped strictly by organization_id.
ai_requirements.implementation_notes:
- The AI service should be framework-agnostic, communicating via standard REST APIs.
- Environment variables should be used for API keys, model names, and service URLs (e.g., AI_SERVICE_URL, AI_API_KEY).
- Testing/Mock Strategy: Provide mock responses in development and testing environments to avoid external API calls and costs. Use unit tests with mocked LLM responses to verify prompt construction and JSON parsing.

cons: Operational overhead: Requires managing, deploying, and monitoring an additional service, database connections, and API keys.
Network latency: Adds an extra HTTP/gRPC hop between the main app and the AI service.
pros: Complete isolation of heavy ML/LLM dependencies from the main application.
Independent scaling: AI workloads can run on GPU-enabled or compute-optimized instances without affecting the main web server.
Language flexibility: Allows using Python (the standard for AI/ML) while the main app can be built in Node.js, Go, or Ruby.
integration_pattern_options.summary: Dedicated AI API service (e.g., a Python FastAPI microservice running LLM/ML logic) that the main application calls.

cons: Blocks application resources: Heavy prompt construction, serialization, or local embedding generation can block the main event loop or consume web server memory.
Dependency bloat: Forces AI SDKs and potential ML libraries into the main application codebase.
pros: Extremely simple architecture: No extra services to deploy or maintain.
Zero network overhead between app and AI logic (except to the LLM provider API).
Shared database access: Direct access to ORM models and database context.
integration_pattern_options.summary: LLM SDK calls directly inside the main application.

cons: Two code paths to maintain and test.
Increased complexity in managing state and job queues (e.g., Redis/BullMQ).
pros: Balanced approach: Simple, low-latency user-facing calls can be done in-app, while heavy schedule optimization or batch recommendation generation runs asynchronously in a background worker.
integration_pattern_options.summary: Light in-app LLM calls for simple tasks + heavy background work in a sidecar or worker.

current_prd.ai_architect_reasoning: The AI architecture is exceptionally well-defined. It includes clear capabilities, a justified integration pattern (separate service), robust multi-tenant guardrails (metadata filtering for vector stores), and detailed API contracts and data model links.
